subject: Data retention: ephemeral trace window & proof-of-delete workflow
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@daedalushealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@daedalushealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data retention: ephemeral trace window & proof-of-delete workflow

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. Our auditors have asked for clarification on how Redwood handles ephemeral inference traces and what evidence we can reasonably expect for a customer-specific retention variance. A few concrete asks from our side:

1) Current default behavior: what exact artifacts are retained for inference traces (request/response text, model version, KV cache metadata, timestamps)?
2) If we need a longer retention window for regulatory audit (up to 24 months), what options exist (config + controls)?
3) Proof-of-delete: can Redwood provide a verifiable proof-of-delete for tenant-scoped traces (e.g., hash manifests, signed S3 lifecycle events, chain-of-custody)?
4) Backups/replicas: do any cross-region backups or analytics pipelines retain the same traces beyond the deletion point?
5) Evidence samples: can you provide a redacted sample trace export and the attestation template your legal team uses?

Procurement is willing to accept a retention carveout for audit purposes, but legal needs explicit evidence artifacts and a short-term attestation. Can you send a suggested approach and sample deliverables?

Appreciate a pragmatic proposal — Lina

Lina Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Daedalus Health

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@daedalushealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data retention: ephemeral trace window & proof-of-delete workflow

Hi Lina —

Thanks — glad the walkthrough was useful. Short answers up-front and then a proposed path:

- Default artifacts: Redwood retains (by default) anonymized inference traces for 90 days: request id, truncated request text (configurable redaction), model id/version, timing metadata, and a KV-cache marker for warm starts. Full user-submitted payloads are not retained beyond the configured TTL unless customer enables longer retention.

- Longer windows: Two supported approaches: (1) Dedicated "tenant retention policy" (reserved capacity customers) where TTL can be configured per-tenant up to customer-requested windows; (2) Hosted customers can opt into an "escrow snapshot" where we produce a time-limited export stored in an encrypted escrow bucket for audit (retained only under an attested carveout).

- Proof-of-delete: We can provide a signed manifest of deleted object keys, a per-object SHA256 digest chain, and S3 lifecycle event logs. For highest assurance, we produce a deletion manifest signed by our KMS key and provide a chain-of-custody CSV.

- Backups/replicas: By default, our analytics pipelines only ingest aggregated telemetry (no raw traces). Raw trace backups are not created unless the customer explicitly enables a snapshot or analytics export. We will confirm specific retention for third-party integrations if you have any enabled on your tenancy.

- Deliverables we can ship right away: redwood-retention-options.pdf (summary of options + costs), sample-redacted-traces.jsonl (redacted sample), chain_of_custody_template.csv, and a draft signed-retention-attestation.docx. I attached the PDF and will follow up with the sample files once legal approves redaction.

Proposal: If Daedalus needs >90 days and <=270 days for audit, we can do a 270-day escrow snapshot with the following commitments:
  * Escrowed snapshot delivered as an encrypted export within 7 business days of request
  * Deletion manifest and KMS-signed hash file on deletion
  * Monthly integrity receipts (hash + timestamp) during the escrow period
  * DocuSign attestation acknowledging the escrow scope and fees

If you need the full 24 months, we can support it but will need a Dedicated contract and a short-term retention fee to cover storage and compliance handling.

If that approach sounds workable, I can loop in Neha and Priyom to draft the attestation and produce the redacted sample.

Best,
Vivek
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Lina Park <lina.park@daedalushealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@daedalushealth.com
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 10:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data retention: ephemeral trace window & proof-of-delete workflow

Vivek —

Thanks for the clear summary. Procurement/legal are likely to accept a 270-day escrow model rather than moving to Dedicated today. Two follow-ups before I greenlight:

1) Cost: our procurement team expects a simple per-GB/month schedule for the escrow (please include an estimate for 10GB/month of redacted traces).
2) Redaction proof: can you provide a sample trace where PII (names, emails, SSNs) has been scrubbed and replaced with deterministic tokens? Legal will review redaction logic.
3) Attestation: we need the attestation to be signable in DocuSign and explicitly reference the SHA256 manifest and the KMS key id.

Also, our SOC 2 auditor would like to see where this maps on the CAIQ control map (retention-related controls) — if you can attach a short CAIQ excerpt or mapping that would save us time.

If you can send the cost estimate + sample by end of week we can route to legal.

-Lina

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@daedalushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data retention: ephemeral trace window & proof-of-delete workflow

Looping internal tech details into the thread so Lina and legal see we have a runnable plan. Quick runbook and artifacts we will produce:

- Runbook: 1) Create per-tenant escrow bucket with SSE-KMS using cust-supplied or Redwood KMS; 2) Export redacted traces (jsonl) from the inference cluster using deterministic tokenization; 3) Generate SHA256 digest per file and produce a signed manifest (manifest.csv) using Redwood signing key; 4) Store export and manifest in escrow bucket with lifecycle rule to auto-delete after 270 days; 5) Produce a chain_of_custody_template.csv mapping export id, operator, timestamp, and verification hash.

- Redaction logic: we use named-entity heuristics + regex fallback to detect email/ssn/phone and replace with stable hashes (token-<sha8>). We will include the sample-redacted-traces.jsonl attachment showing before/after for 8 lines (no real PII).

- Costing: rough estimate for 10GB/month of redacted traces (compressed) on the escrow path: $0.12/GB/month storage + $50 one-time export handling fee. We will formalize in the quote.

Attachments included in this message: sample-redacted-traces.jsonl, chain_of_custody_template.csv.

Priyom — can you confirm the KMS key id we will surface in the attestation and whether the signed manifest will use our signing key or an HSM-backed signature?

-Neha
